subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 56-year-old woman with acute myeloid leukemia receives cytarabine (ara-C), a pyrimidine analog. Her bone marrow blasts arrest in S phase and undergo apoptosis after the drug is incorporated into newly synthesized DNA.
question: Which of the following best explains the cytotoxic effect of cytarabine?

options.text: Incorporation into DNA with a modified 3'-OH that prevents addition of the next nucleotide

explanation_correct: Nucleoside analogs such as cytarabine are incorporated into the growing DNA chain but carry a modified 3'-OH, so the next deoxynucleotide cannot be added. This chain termination blocks DNA synthesis, which is why such drugs preferentially kill rapidly dividing cells.

explanation_incorrect.B: Ribonucleotide reductase is inhibited by hydroxyurea.
explanation_incorrect.C: Dihydrofolate reductase is inhibited by methotrexate.
explanation_incorrect.E: Irinotecan and topotecan inhibit topoisomerase I and act by a different mechanism.

educationalObjective: Nucleoside analogs with an altered 3'-OH terminate DNA chain elongation.
